original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Sharp total and irreducible joint-image dimensions of a complete no-edge binary rank-one idempotent pool whose off-diagonal pattern space has dimension 4.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package stays in the abelian F2 rank-one idempotent model and answers the open question of #7094: whether a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 can act irreducibly in joint-image dimension 6 or more. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921, #6962, and #7094.
bottleneck_link: Side result. The scalar pool bound does not by itself price a word, so the original native acceptance gate remains unmet. A later word argument can no longer look for an irreducible pattern-dimension-4 image of dimension 6 or more. The selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the all-width total bound 6 and the reducibility of dimension 6 are checked, and the #7094 dimension-5 witness has been rechecked. Do not start a pattern-dimension-5 classification or a word synthesis.
evidence: PROOF.md shows that every complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 has joint image of dimension at most 6, and that dimension 6 is reducible. verify.py repeats the 5005-subset census, the GL(3,2) triple census, the three dimension-6 witnesses, and the #7094 dimension-5 irreducibility check.

ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the case analysis, the finite censuses, and the package verifier. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 5 still have total joint image at most 6, and can its irreducible image exceed 5?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dimension-4 census and the hyperplane argument both use dim P = 4. Pattern dimension 5 is the first case this proof does not bound, while the parity construction already reaches total image 6.
open_questions.first_step: Exhibit one unit-free pattern space of dimension 5 whose complete pool has image rank 7, or extend the active-set argument without a 3-dimensional hyperplane.
open_questions.blocked_by: F2^5 has more than six nonzero vectors, so the six-point partition does not exhaust a larger pool.

open_questions.question: Is every dimension-6 no-edge pool a coordinate permutation of one of the three witnesses?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dimension bound does not identify the pools. A coordinate list would show whether any further reducible geometry exists at the bound.
open_questions.first_step: Match each T-space, or each normal-form block, to a fixed pair of coordinate sets and record the stabilizer.
open_questions.blocked_by: The case split names the geometries but does not enumerate coordinate placements.

open_questions.question: After a valid relation, cube-span, and coordinate-call split, does irreducible dimension at most 5 change a three-relation paid-rank obstruction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is still question 1 of #6921. The scalar bound does not by itself decide whether a concrete word saves a factor.
open_questions.first_step: State the exact split hypotheses from the predecessor word reductions, then account for endpoints and paid rank only where those hypotheses hold.
open_questions.blocked_by: The word-reduction hypotheses are not reproved in this package.
